en: I meditate upon the beautiful Aṭṭāla, adorned by arms as lovely as the bow of Mount Kailāsa, which has swallowed up the entire world. 1.
I meditate upon the bearer of the crescent moon, whose neck is stained by the mass of radiance from the *kālakūṭa* poison,
who wears the crescent on his crest, and who is as beautiful as a watchtower.
I meditate upon the one who is the death of Death, who transcends all parts yet possesses all parts, who is partless, who is praised by the Lord of Kamalā, and who is as beautiful as a turret. 3.

I meditate upon him who has half his body as his beloved, whose limbs are lovely, who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion, who destroys the defects of the sins of the Kali age, and who is beautiful with his crown. 4.

I meditate upon the Lord who is the sovereign of the Kadamba forest, the celestial wish-fulfilling tree for desired objects, the subduer of Kama, the Supreme Ruler, who is as beautiful as a lofty palace tower. || 5 ||
By whom many cosmic eggs were created through his illusory power (māyā), protected, and finally destroyed; to that one who is as beautiful as a watchtower (aṭṭāla), I bow.
I meditate upon the beautiful pinnacle of the temple, the cause of all worlds, which is intent on destroying the lotus-like misfortunes and sins that cause suffering to its own devotees.
I meditate upon the one who is the family deity of the kings born of the Kulaśekhara lineage,
who is the fullness of consciousness and bliss, and who is as beautiful as the Aṭṭāla temple.
May this excellent *Aṣṭaka* of Śambhu, the Hero of the Fort (*Aṭṭālavīra*), which bestows desired objects, immediately grant supreme prosperity to those who recite or hear it. (9)
Thus ends "The Eight Verses on Aṭṭālasundara" composed by Vikrama Pāṇḍya within the *Śrī-Hālāsya-Māhātmya*.
